    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
      const o0 = -ROAD_HALF_WIDTH + 0.6 + i * 1.0;
      pushPathPatch(verts, stop + 0.8, stop + 4.3, o0, o0 + 0.5, 0.03, paint);
    }
  }
  // dashes
  for (let s = 0; s < SQ_C; s += 6) {
    if (SQ_STOPS.some((stop) => s > stop - 2 && s < stop + 6)) continue;
    pushPathPatch(verts, s, s + 2, -0.075, 0.075, 0.03, paint);
  }
  // poles
  for (const lamp of SQ_LAMPS) {
    pushBox(verts, [lamp.x - 0.1, 0, lamp.z - 0.1], [lamp.x + 0.1, 4, lamp.z + 0.1], [0.4, 0.4, 0.42]);
  }
  return verts;
}

function squareScene(): SceneDef {
  return {
    c: SQ_C,
    obstacles: SQ_STOPS.map((s) => ({ s })),
    lamps: SQ_LAMPS,
    buildStatic: squareStatic,
    carPose(car) {
      const p = squarePathPoint(car.s);
      const o = 2 * (1 - 2 * car.lateral);
      const yaw = Math.atan2(4 * car.lateralVel, Math.max(car.v, 1));
      return {
        x: p.x + p.rx * o,
        y: 0.02,
        z: p.z + p.rz * o,
        angle: Math.atan2(-p.hz, p.hx) + yaw,
        pitch: 0,
      };
    },
  };
}

export const SCENES: SceneDef[] = [ringScene(), squareScene()];

```ts
function squarePathPoint(s: number): { x: number; z: number; hx: number; hz: number; rx: number; rz: number } {
  const wrapped = ((s % SQ_C) + SQ_C) % SQ_C;
  const seg = Math.min(Math.floor(wrapped / SQ_SEG), 3);
  const d = wrapped - seg * SQ_SEG;
  const side = SQ_SIDES[seg];
  if (d <= SQ_STRAIGHT) {
    return { x: side.ex + d * side.hx, z: side.ez + d * side.hz, hx: side.hx, hz: side.hz, rx: side.rx, rz: side.rz };
  }
  const phi = (d - SQ_STRAIGHT) / SQ_CORNER_R;
  const ax = side.ex + SQ_STRAIGHT * side.hx;
  const az = side.ez + SQ_STRAIGHT * side.hz;
  const sin = Math.sin(phi);
  const cos = Math.cos(phi);
  return {
    x: ax + SQ_CORNER_R * (sin * side.hx + (1 - cos) * side.rx),
    z: az + SQ_CORNER_R * (sin * side.hz + (1 - cos) * side.rz),
    hx: cos * side.hx + sin * side.rx,
    hz: cos * side.hz + sin * side.rz,
    rx: side.rx,
    rz: side.rz,
  };
}

export class Renderer {
  private readonly device, context, format;
  private vertexBuffer: GPUBuffer;
  private readonly cameraBuffer, drawBuffer, pipeline, bindGroup;
  private readonly carVertexCount: number;
  private readonly lampFirstVertex: number;
  private readonly lampVertexCount: number;

  private cars: Car[];
  private carParams: IdmParams[];
  private def: SceneDef;
  private scene: number;
  private builtCarLength: number;
  private builtDayMode: boolean;
  private lightClock = 0;
  private readonly orbit: OrbitCamera;
  private depthTexture?: GPUTexture;
  private configured = false;
  private animationFrame?: number;
  private lastTime?: number;
  private accumulator = 0;

  constructor(canvas, gpu, gui) {
    ...device/context/format...
    this.scene = gui.settings.scene;
    this.def = SCENES[this.scene - 1];
    this.carVerts = buildCarMesh(gui.settings.carLength);
    this.lampVerts = buildLampMesh();
    this.carVertexCount = this.carVerts.length / 9;
    this.lampFirstVertex = this.carVertexCount;
    this.lampVertexCount = this.lampVerts.length / 9;
    this.staticFirstVertex = this.lampFirstVertex + this.lampVertexCount;
    const staticVerts = this.def.buildStatic(this.palette());
    this.staticVertexCount = staticVerts.length / 9;
    this.vertexBuffer = createBufferWithData(device, 'scene vertices', new Float32Array([...this.carVerts, ...this.lampVerts, ...staticVerts]), GPUBufferUsage.VERTEX);
    ...camera/draw buffers (draw: DRAW_STRIDE * TOTAL_SLOTS), layout, pipeline, bindGroup...
    this.resetCars();
    this.builtCarLength = ...; this.builtDayMode = ...; this.orbit = ...;
  }

  start/stop/destroy (vertexBuffer destroy fine)

  private palette(): Palette {...}
  private currentPhase(): LightPhase {...}

  /** Switches the active scene: rebuilds the static mesh and restarts traffic. */
  private applyScene(scene: number): void {
    this.scene = scene;
    this.def = SCENES[scene - 1];
    const staticVerts = this.def.buildStatic(this.palette());
    this.staticVertexCount = staticVerts.length / 9;
    this.vertexBuffer.destroy();
    this.vertexBuffer = createBufferWithData(this.device, 'scene vertices', new Float32Array([...this.carVerts, ...this.lampVerts, ...staticVerts]), GPUBufferUsage.VERTEX);
    this.resetCars();
    this.lightClock = 0;
  }

  /** Places all cars at their start positions for the current scene. */
  private resetCars(): void {
    const c = this.def.c;
    this.cars = this.gui.settings.cars.map((params, i) => ({
      s: START_FRACTIONS[i % START_FRACTIONS.length] * c,
      v: params.v0,
      a: 0,
      lane: START_LANES[i % START_LANES.length],
      lateral: START_LANES[i % START_LANES.length],
      lateralVel: 0,
      laneFrom: START_LANES[i % START_LANES.length],
      laneProgress: 1,
      cooldown: 0,
    }));
    this.carParams = [...this.gui.settings.cars];
  }

  syncCars (same)
  leaderGap (CIRCUMFERENCE → this.def.c)

  render:
    if (this.gui.settings.scene !== this.scene) this.applyScene(this.gui.settings.scene);
    ...resize...
    sim: stepRing(this.cars, this.gui.settings.cars, this.def.c, carLength, SIM_STEP, clear ? NO_OBSTACLES : this.def.obstacles)
    car mesh rebuild: offset 0 (carFirstVertex gone → 0) + update this.carVerts!
      this.carVerts = buildCarMesh(this.builtCarLength);

}

Corners must be CCW seen from outside. */\nexport function pushQuad(out: number[], corners: [Vec3, Vec3, Vec3, Vec3], color: Vec3): void {\n  const [a, b, c, d] = corners;\n  const ux = b[0] - a[0];\n  const uy = b[1] - a[1];\n  const uz = b[2] - a[2];\n  const vx = c[0] - a[0];\n  const vy = c[1] - a[1];\n  const vz = c[2] - a[2];\n  const nx = uy * vz - uz * vy;\n  const ny = uz * vx - ux * vz;\n  const nz = ux * vy - uy * vx;\n  const len = Math.hypot(nx, ny, nz);\n  for (const p of [a, b, c, a, c, d]) {\n    out.push(p[0], p[1], p[2], nx / len, ny / len, nz / len, color[0], color[1], color[2]);\n  }\n}\n\n/** Appends a box (5 faces, bottom omitted: the camera stays above) to a vertex list. */\nexport function pushBox(out: number[], min: Vec3, max: Vec3, color: Vec3): void {\n  const [x0, y0, z0] = min;\n  const [x1, y1, z1] = max;\n  pushQuad(out, [[x0, y1, z0], [x0, y1, z1], [x1, y1, z1], [x1, y1, z0]], color); // top\n  pushQuad(out, [[x1, y0, z1], [x1, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z0], [x1, y1, z1]], color); // +x\n  pushQuad(out, [[x0, y0, z0], [x0, y0, z1], [x0, y1, z1], [x0, y1, z0]], color); // −x\n  pushQuad(out, [[x0, y0, z1], [x1, y0, z1], [x1, y1, z1], [x0, y1, z1]], color); // +z\n  pushQuad(out, [[x1, y0, z0], [x0, y0, z0], [x0, y1, z0], [x1, y1, z0]], color); // −z\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Scene 1: the ring with a bridge.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst TRACK_RADIUS = 40;\nconst ROAD_HALF_WIDTH = 4;\nconst RING_C = 2 * Math.PI * TRACK_RADIUS;\n/** Arc position of the stop line / pedestrian crossing (quarter lap, nearest the camera). */\nconst STOP_S = RING_C / 4;\n/** The signal hangs just inside the inner road edge at the stop line. */\nconst RING_LAMP = {\n  x: (TRACK_RADIUS - ROAD_HALF_WIDTH - 1.2) * Math.cos(STOP_S / TRACK_RADIUS),\n  z: (TRACK_RADIUS - ROAD_HALF_WIDTH - 1.2) * Math.sin(STOP_S / TRACK_RADIUS),\n};\n\n/** The bridge is a raised-cosine bump on the far side of the ring (clear of the cars' start and the crossing). */\nconst BRIDGE_LENGTH = 60; // m along the arc\nconst BRIDGE_HEIGHT = 4; // m\nconst BRIDGE_START = (3 * RING_C) / 4 - BRIDGE_LENGTH / 2;\n\n/** Road surface height above the ground at arc position s (0 off the bridge). */\nfunction roadHeight(s: number): number {\n  if (s < BRIDGE_START || s > BRIDGE_START + BRIDGE_LENGTH) return 0;\n  const u = (s - BRIDGE_START) / BRIDGE_LENGTH;\n  return (BRIDGE_HEIGHT / 2) * (1 - Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * u));\n}\n\n/** Slope (dh/ds) of the road at arc position s. */\nfunction roadGrade(s: number): number {\n  if (s < BRIDGE_START || s > BRIDGE_START + BRIDGE_LENGTH) return 0;\n  const u = (s - BRIDGE_START) / BRIDGE_LENGTH;\n  return ((BRIDGE_HEIGHT * Math.PI) / BRIDGE_LENGTH) * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * u);\n}\n\n/** Appends a rectangular road patch covering arc [s0, s1] and radius [r0, r1]. */\nfunction pushRoadPatch(out: number[], s0: number, s1: number, r0: number, r1: number, color: Vec3): void {\n  // ponytail: a single straight quad per patch; over a few meters of arc it sags ~4 cm off the\n  // circle, invisible at this zoom. Segment along the arc if patches get much longer.\n  const at = (s: number, r: number): Vec3 => {\n    const theta = s / TRACK_RADIUS;\n    return [r * Math.cos(theta), 0.03, r * Math.sin(theta)];\n  };\n  pushQuad(out, [at(s0, r0), at(s1, r0), at(s1, r1), at(s0, r1)], color);\n}\n\n/** Appends a lane-divider dash centered between the two lanes, following the road height. */\nfunction pushLaneDash(out: number[], s0: number, s1: number, color: Vec3): void {\n  const r0 = TRACK_RADIUS - 0.075;\n  const r1 = TRACK_RADIUS + 0.075;\n  const at = (s: number, r: number): Vec3 => {\n    const theta = s / TRACK_RADIUS;\n    return [r * Math.cos(theta), 0.03 + roadHeight(s), r * Math.sin(theta)];\n  };\n  pushQuad(out, [at(s0, r0), at(s1, r0), at(s1, r1), at(s0, r1)], color);\n}\n\n/** Ground plane + ring road + crossing paint + light pole, vertex colors baked in. */\nfunction ringStatic(palette: Palette): number[] {\n  const verts: number[] = [];\n  const G = 300;\n  pushQuad(verts, [[-G, 0, -G], [-G, 0, G], [G, 0, G], [G, 0, -G]], palette.ground);\n\n  const asphalt = palette.asphalt;\n  const wall = palette.wall;\n  const inner = TRACK_RADIUS - ROAD_HALF_WIDTH;\n  const outer = TRACK_RADIUS + ROAD_HALF_WIDTH;\n  const SEGMENTS = 128;\n  for (let i = 0; i < SEGMENTS; i++) {\n    const t0 = (i / SEGMENTS) * 2 * Math.PI;\n    const t1 = ((i + 1) / SEGMENTS) * 2 * Math.PI;\n    const h0 = 0.02 + roadHeight(t0 * TRACK_RADIUS);\n    const h1 = 0.02 + roadHeight(t1 * TRACK_RADIUS);\n    pushQuad(\n      verts,\n      [\n        [inner * Math.cos(t0), h0, inner * Math.sin(t0)],\n        [inner * Math.cos(t1), h1, inner * Math.sin(t1)],\n        [outer * Math.cos(t1), h1, outer * Math.sin(t1)],\n        [outer * Math.cos(t0), h0, outer * Math.sin(t0)],\n      ],\n      asphalt,\n    );\n    // Side walls under the elevated section so the bridge reads as solid.\n    if (h0 > 0.05 || h1 > 0.05) {\n      pushQuad(\n        verts,\n        [\n          [outer * Math.cos(t0), 0, outer * Math.sin(t0)],\n          [outer * Math.cos(t0), h0, outer * Math.sin(t0)],\n          [outer * Math.cos(t1), h1, outer * Math.sin(t1)],\n          [outer * Math.cos(t1), 0, outer * Math.sin(t1)],\n        ],\n        wall,\n      );\n      pushQuad(\n        verts,\n        [\n          [inner * Math.cos(t0), h0, inner * Math.sin(t0)],\n          [inner * Math.cos(t0), 0, inner * Math.sin(t0)],\n          [inner * Math.cos(t1), 0, inner * Math.sin(t1)],\n          [inner * Math.cos(t1), h1, inner * Math.sin(t1)],\n        ],\n        wall,\n      );\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Solid stop line across the lane, then a zebra crossing after it: stripes run\n  // parallel to travel, packed across the lane width.\n  const paint: Vec3 = [0.9, 0.9, 0.9];\n  pushRoadPatch(verts, STOP_S - 0.125, STOP_S + 0.125, inner, outer, paint);\n  for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {\n    const r0 = inner + 0.6 + i * 1.0;\n    pushRoadPatch(verts, STOP_S + 0.8, STOP_S + 4.3, r0, r0 + 0.5, paint);\n  }\n\n  // Dashed divider between the lanes, skipping the crossing.\n  for (let s = 0; s < RING_C; s += 6) {\n    if (s > STOP_S - 2 && s < STOP_S + 6) continue;\n    pushLaneDash(verts, s, s + 2, paint);\n  }\n\n  // Traffic-light pole beside the road, tall enough for the three lamps.\n  pushBox(\n    verts,\n    [RING_LAMP.x - 0.1, 0, RING_LAMP.z - 0.1],\n    [RING_LAMP.x + 0.1, 4, RING_LAMP.z + 0.1],\n    [0.4, 0.4, 0.42],\n  );\n  return verts;\n}\n\nfunction ringScene(): SceneDef {\n  return {\n    c: RING_C,\n    obstacles: [{ s: STOP_S }],\n    lamps: [RING_LAMP],\n    buildStatic: ringStatic,\n    carPose(car) {\n      const theta = car.s / TRACK_RADIUS;\n      // Lane centers are 2 m either side of the track radius; lateral eases between them.\n      const r = TRACK_RADIUS - 2 + 4 * car.lateral;\n      // While sliding sideways, yaw the body along the actual velocity direction.\n      const yaw = Math.atan2(4 * car.lateralVel, Math.max(car.v, 1));\n      return {\n        x: r * Math.cos(theta),\n        y: 0.02 + roadHeight(car.s),\n        z: r * Math.sin(theta),\n        angle: -theta - Math.PI / 2 + yaw,\n        pitch: Math.atan(roadGrade(car.s)),\n      };\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Scene 2: a square loop, clockwise. 4 straights, 4 rounded corners, and a\n// stop line + zebra + traffic light at the end of each straight.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nconst SQ_STRAIGHT = 100; // m per side\nconst SQ_CORNER_R = 8; // m, centerline corner radius\nconst SQ_HALF = SQ_STRAIGHT / 2 + SQ_CORNER_R;\nconst SQ_SEG = SQ_STRAIGHT + (Math.PI / 2) * SQ_CORNER_R;\nconst SQ_C = 4 * SQ_SEG;\n/** Stop line arc offset within each side: 5 m before the corner. */\nconst SQ_STOP_OFFSET = SQ_STRAIGHT - 5;\n\n// Clockwise sides: straight start point, heading h, and right normal r (toward the loop center).\nconst SQ_SIDES = [\n  { ex: -SQ_STRAIGHT / 2, ez: -SQ_HALF, hx: 1, hz: 0, rx: 0, rz: 1 },\n  { ex: SQ_HALF, ez: -SQ_STRAIGHT / 2, hx: 0, hz: 1, rx: -1, rz: 0 },\n  { ex: SQ_STRAIGHT / 2, ez: SQ_HALF, hx: -1, hz: 0, rx: 0, rz: -1 },\n  { ex: -SQ_HALF, ez: SQ_STRAIGHT / 2, hx: 0, hz: -1, rx: 1, rz: 0 },\n];\n\ninterface PathPoint {\n  x: number;\n  z: number;\n  hx: number; // heading (unit)\n  hz: number;\n  rx: number; // right normal (unit, toward the turn's center)\n  rz: number;\n}\n\n/** Centerline point + heading + right normal at arc position s on the square loop. */\nfunction squarePathPoint(s: number): PathPoint {\n  const wrapped = ((s % SQ_C) + SQ_C) % SQ_C;\n  const seg = Math.min(Math.floor(wrapped / SQ_SEG), 3);\n  const d = wrapped - seg * SQ_SEG;\n  const side = SQ_SIDES[seg];\n  if (d <= SQ_STRAIGHT) {\n    return {\n      x: side.ex + d * side.hx,\n      z: side.ez + d * side.hz,\n      hx: side.hx,\n      hz: side.hz,\n      rx: side.rx,\n      rz: side.rz,\n    };\n  }\n  // Rounded corner: quarter circle turning right, from heading h to heading r.\n  const phi = (d - SQ_STRAIGHT) / SQ_CORNER_R;\n  const ax = side.ex + SQ_STRAIGHT * side.hx;\n  const az = side.ez + SQ_STRAIGHT * side.hz;\n  const sin = Math.sin(phi);\n  const cos = Math.cos(phi);\n  return {\n    x: ax + SQ_CORNER_R * (sin * side.hx + (1 - cos) * side.rx),\n    z: az + SQ_CORNER_R * (sin * side.hz + (1 - cos) * side.rz),\n    hx: cos * side.hx + sin * side.rx,\n    hz: cos * side.hz + sin * side.rz,\n    rx: -sin * side.hx + cos * side.rx,\n    rz: -sin * side.hz + cos * side.rz,\n  };\n}\n\n/** Appends a path patch covering arc [s0, s1] and lateral offsets [o0, o1] (o+ = toward loop center). */\nfunction pushPathPatch(\n  out: number[],\n  s0: number,\n  s1: number,\n  o0: number,\n  o1: number,\n  y: number,\n  color: Vec3,\n): void {\n  const at = (s: number, o: number): Vec3 => {\n    const p = squarePathPoint(s);\n    return [p.x + p.rx * o, y, p.z + p.rz * o];\n  };\n  pushQuad(out, [at(s0, o1), at(s1, o1), at(s1, o0), at(s0, o0)], color);\n}\n\nconst SQ_STOPS = [0, 1, 2, 3].map((k) => k * SQ_SEG + SQ_STOP_OFFSET);\n/** Poles just inside the inner road edge at each stop line. */\nconst SQ_LAMPS = SQ_STOPS.map((s) => {\n  const p = squarePathPoint(s);\n  return {\n    x: p.x + p.rx * (ROAD_HALF_WIDTH + 1.2),\n    z: p.z + p.rz * (ROAD_HALF_WIDTH + 1.2),\n  };\n});\n\nfunction squareStatic(palette: Palette): number[] {\n  const verts: number[] = [];\n  const G = 300;\n  pushQuad(verts, [[-G, 0, -G], [-G, 0, G], [G, 0, G], [G, 0, -G]], palette.ground);\n\n  // Road ribbon, 1 m patches so the corner arcs are smooth.\n  for (let s = 0; s < SQ_C; s += 1) {\n    pushPathPatch(verts, s, Math.min(s + 1, SQ_C), -ROAD_HALF_WIDTH, ROAD_HALF_WIDTH, 0.02, palette.asphalt);\n  }\n\n  const paint: Vec3 = [0.9, 0.9, 0.9];\n  // Stop lines + zebra crossings (stripes parallel to travel) at every intersection.\n  for (const stop of SQ_STOPS) {\n    pushPathPatch(verts, stop - 0.125, stop + 0.125, -ROAD_HALF_WIDTH, ROAD_HALF_WIDTH, 0.03, paint);\n    for (let i = 0; i < 7; i++) {\n      const o0 = -ROAD_HALF_WIDTH + 0.6 + i * 1.0;\n      pushPathPatch(verts, stop + 0.8, stop + 4.3, o0, o0 + 0.5, 0.03, paint);\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Dashed lane divider, skipping the crossings.\n  for (let s = 0; s < SQ_C; s += 6) {\n    if (SQ_STOPS.some((stop) => s > stop - 2 && s < stop + 6)) continue;\n    pushPathPatch(verts, s, s + 2, -0.075, 0.075, 0.03, paint);\n  }\n\n  // Signal poles.\n  for (const lamp of SQ_LAMPS) {\n    pushBox(verts, [lamp.x - 0.1, 0, lamp.z - 0.1], [lamp.x + 0.1, 4, lamp.z + 0.1], [0.4, 0.4, 0.42]);\n  }\n  return verts;\n}\n\nfunction squareScene(): SceneDef {\n  return {\n    c: SQ_C,\n    obstacles: SQ_STOPS.map((s) => ({ s })),\n    lamps: SQ_LAMPS,\n    buildStatic: squareStatic,\n    carPose(car) {\n      const p = squarePathPoint(car.s);\n      // Lane centers are 2 m either side of the centerline (o+ = inner lane, toward the center).\n      const o = 2 * (1 - 2 * car.lateral);\n      const yaw = Math.atan2(4 * car.lateralVel, Math.max(car.v, 1));\n      return {\n        x: p.x + p.rx * o,\n        y: 0.02,\n        z: p.z + p.rz * o,\n        angle: Math.atan2(-p.hz, p.hx) + yaw,\n        pitch: 0,\n      };\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nexport const SCENES: SceneDef[] = [ringScene(), squareScene()];\n",

Before building, let me sanity-check the square path math with a quick script — corner continuity (end of arc == start of next straight), lane offset normal. Cheap and worth it since I derived it by hand:

- For each side k: pathPoint at end of arc (d = SEG) == pathPoint at start of next side (d=0 of k+1).
- |heading| = 1 throughout.
- Offset point stays on road (|offset| = 2).

**8. stepRoad**

```ts
export function stepRoad(road: Road, cars: Car[], params: IdmParams[], carLength: number, dt: number): void {
  const L = road.length;
  const accels = cars.map((car, i) => {
    const lane = road.lanes[car.lane];
    const dir = lane.direction;
    let accel = idmAcceleration(car.v, 1e6, 0, params[i]);
    let gap = Infinity, vLeader = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < cars.length; j++) {
      if (j === i || cars[j].lane !== car.lane) continue;
      const d = (cars[j].s - car.s) * dir; // distance ahead in travel direction
      if (d > 0 && d < gap) { gap = d; vLeader = cars[j].v; }
    }
    if (Number.isFinite(gap)) accel = Math.min(accel, idmAcceleration(car.v, gap - carLength, car.v - vLeader, params[i]));
    // End of the open road is a permanent stop sign.
    const dEnd = dir > 0 ? L - car.s : car.s;
    accel = Math.min(accel, idmAcceleration(car.v, dEnd - carLength / 2, car.v, params[i]));
    return accel;
  });
  updateRoadLanes(road, cars, params, carLength);
  for (let i = 0; i < cars.length; i++) {
    const car = cars[i];
    car.a = accels[i];
    car.v = Math.max(0, car.v + car.a * dt);
    car.s = clamp(car.s + road.lanes[car.lane].direction * car.v * dt, 0, L);
    car.cooldown = Math.max(0, car.cooldown - dt);
    // same cosine lateral easing
    ...
  }
}
```

nearestInLane for road (no wrap, directional):
```ts
function nearestOnRoad(cars, me, laneIndex, dir, ahead): {index, gap, v} | null {
  let best = null;
  for j: if j===me || cars[j].lane !== laneIndex continue;
  const d = (cars[j].s - cars[me].s) * dir;
  const gap = ahead ? d : -d;
  if (gap > 0 && (best === null || gap < best.gap)) best = {index: j, gap, v: cars[j].v};
}
```
ahead: cars in front in travel direction: dir=+1 → j.s > i.s → d>0 ✓; behind: gap = −d > 0 → j behind ✓.

idm.ts refactor of the lateral block:

```ts
/** Advances one car's lane-change slide and cooldown by dt (cosine-eased S-curve). */
export function advanceLateral(car: Car, dt: number): void {
  car.cooldown = Math.max(0, car.cooldown - dt);
  if (car.laneProgress < 1) {
    car.laneProgress = Math.min(1, car.laneProgress + dt / LANE_CHANGE_TIME);
    const p = car.laneProgress;
    car.lateral = car.laneFrom + (car.lane - car.laneFrom) * (0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos(Math.PI * p));
    car.lateralVel =
      ((car.lane - car.laneFrom) * 0.5 * Math.PI * Math.sin(Math.PI * p)) / LANE_CHANGE_TIME;
    if (p === 1) car.lateralVel = 0;
  } else {
    car.lateralVel = 0;
  }
}
```

- **`src/sim/road.ts`** — `Road` class: any centerline path (straight/arc/S-curve), N forward + M backward lanes (0 backward = one-way), yellow line at offset 0 separating directions. `stepRoad` = IDM on an open segment (no wrap), with the road ends acting as permanent stop signs, and MOBIL lane changes between adjacent same-direction lanes.

gap: number; v: number } | null {\n  let best: { index: number; gap: number; v: number } | null = null;\n  for (let j = 0; j < cars.length; j++) {\n    if (j === me || cars[j].lane !== laneIndex) continue;\n    const d = (cars[j].s - cars[me].s) * direction;\n    const gap = ahead ? d : -d;\n    if (gap > 0 && (best === null || gap < best.gap)) best = { index: j, gap, v: cars[j].v };\n  }\n  return best;\n}\n\n/** Lanes a car on `laneIndex` may change to: adjacent lanes going the same direction. */\nfunction adjacentLanes(road: Road, laneIndex: number): number[] {\n  const lane = road.lanes[laneIndex];\n  const targets: number[] = [];\n  road.lanes.forEach((other, i) => {\n    if (i !== laneIndex && other.direction === lane.direction && Math.abs(other.offset - lane.offset) === LANE_WIDTH) {\n      targets.push(i);\n    }\n  });\n  return targets;\n}\n\nfunction accelToward(car: Car, leader: { gap: number; v: number } | null, carLength: number, p: IdmParams): number {\n  return leader\n    ? idmAcceleration(car.v, leader.gap - carLength, car.v - leader.v, p)\n    : idmAcceleration(car.v, 1e6, 0, p);\n}\n\n/** MOBIL-lite lane changes on the road: same rules as the ring, adjacent same-direction lanes only. */\nfunction updateRoadLanes(road: Road, cars: Car[], params: IdmParams[], carLength: number): void {\n  for (let i = 0; i < cars.length; i++) {\n    const car = cars[i];\n    if (car.cooldown > 0) continue;\n    const dir = road.lanes[car.lane].direction;\n    const accelHere = accelToward(car, nearestOnRoad(cars, i, car.lane, dir, true), carLength, params[i]);\n    let bestTarget = -1;\n    let bestAccel = accelHere + DELTA_A;\n    for (const target of adjacentLanes(road, car.lane)) {\n      const accelThere = accelToward(car, nearestOnRoad(cars, i, target, dir, true), carLength, params[i]);\n      if (accelThere <= bestAccel) continue;\n      // Safety first: no hard braking for me or for the car behind me in the target lane.\n      if (accelThere < -B_SAFE) continue;\n      const follower = nearestOnRoad(cars, i, target, dir, false);\n      if (follower) {\n        const followerAccel = idmAcceleration(\n          follower.v,\n          follower.gap - carLength,\n          follower.v - car.v,\n          params[follower.index],\n        );\n        if (followerAccel < -B_SAFE) continue;\n      }\n      bestTarget = target;\n      bestAccel = accelThere;\n    }\n    if (bestTarget >= 0) {\n      car.lane = bestTarget;\n      car.cooldown = LANE_CHANGE_COOLDOWN;\n      car.laneFrom = car.lateral;\n      car.laneProgress = 0;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Advances every car on the road by one fixed step. }

function ringTopology(c: number) {
  return {
    step: (cars, params, carLength, dt, obstacles) => stepRing(cars, params, c, carLength, dt, obstacles),
    leaderGap: (cars, i, carLength) => {
      const car = cars[i];
      let gap = Infinity;
      for (let j = 0; j < cars.length; j++) {
        if (j === i || cars[j].lane !== car.lane) continue;
        gap = Math.min(gap, (((cars[j].s - car.s) % c) + c) % c);
      }
      return Number.isFinite(gap) ? gap - carLength : null;
    },
    findSpawnSlot: (cars, carParams, params, carLength) => { ...moved from renderer, c in closure... },
  };
}

export const scene3State: { road: Road | null } = { road: null };

function requireRoad(): Road {
  if (!scene3State.road) throw new Error('scene 3 road not built');
  return scene3State.road;
}

function roadScene(): SceneDef {
  return {
    get c() { return requireRoad().length; },
    obstacles: [],
    lamps: [],
    buildStatic: (palette) => buildRoadStatic(requireRoad(), palette),
    carPose: (car) => roadCarPose(requireRoad(), car),

function buildRoadStatic(road: Road, palette: Palette): number[] {
  const verts: number[] = [];
  const G = 300;
  pushQuad(verts, [[-G, 0, -G], [-G, 0, G], [G, 0, G], [G, 0, -G]], palette.ground);

  const f = road.config.lanesForward;
  const b = road.config.lanesBackward;
  const oMin = -4 * b;
  const oMax = 4 * f;
  // Road ribbon in 1 m patches.
  for (let s = 0; s < road.length; s += 1) {
    pushPathPatch(verts, road, s, Math.min(s + 1, road.length), oMin, oMax, 0.02, palette.asphalt);
  }
  // Solid yellow line separating the directions (left edge on a one-way road).
  const yellow: Vec3 = [0.8, 0.65, 0.1];
  for (let s = 0; s < road.length; s += 2) {
    pushPathPatch(verts, road, s, Math.min(s + 2, road.length), -0.075, 0.075, 0.03, yellow);
  }
  // White dashes between same-direction lanes.
  const paint: Vec3 = [0.9, 0.9, 0.9];
  const dashOffsets: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 1; i < f; i++) dashOffsets.push(4 * i);
  for (let j = 1; j < b; j++) dashOffsets.push(-4 * j);
  for (const o of dashOffsets) {
    for (let s = 0; s < road.length; s += 6) {
      pushPathPatch(verts, road, s, Math.min(s + 2, road.length), o - 0.075, o + 0.075, 0.03, paint);
    }
  }
  // Stop lines at the travel end of each direction + stop-sign posts.
  ...

roadCarPose(road, car):
```ts
function roadCarPose(road: Road, car: Car) {
  const fromLane = road.lanes[Math.round(car.laneFrom)];
  const toLane = road.lanes[car.lane];
  const span = car.lane - car.laneFrom;
  const t = span === 0 ? 1 : (car.lateral - car.laneFrom) / span;
  const offset = fromLane.offset + (toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * t;
  const offsetVel = span === 0 ? 0 : ((toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * car.lateralVel) / span;
  const dir = toLane.direction;
  const p = road.point(car.s);
  const yaw = Math.atan2(offsetVel * dir, Math.max(car.v, 1));
  return {
    x: p.x + p.rx * offset,
    y: 0.02,
    z: p.z + p.rz * offset,
    angle: Math.atan2(-p.hz, p.hx) + (dir < 0 ? Math.PI : 0) + yaw,
    pitch: 0,
  };
}
```
Wait — yaw sign: velocity = v·t̂ + offsetVel·r̂ where t̂ = dir·ĥ; right of travel = dir·r̂. v_travel_right = offsetVel·dir? velocity lateral component along r̂ is offsetVel; along right-of-travel (dir·r̂) is offsetVel·dir... wait: offsetVel·r̂ = (offsetVel·dir)·(dir·r̂) since dir² = 1 ✓. So velocity = v·t̂ + (offsetVel·dir)·(right of travel) → yaw = atan2(offsetVel·dir, v) ✓ as written.

Also check angle for backward: base angle atan2(−hz, hx) is the FORWARD path heading; backward car faces −h: angle + π ✓.

Hmm — one subtlety: `car.laneFrom` is integer-valued in practice (cooldown > slide time). Math.round guards float dust ✓.

```ts
/** Appends a path patch covering arc [s0, s1] and lateral offsets [o0, o1] (o+ = toward loop center). */
function pushPathPatch(
  out: number[],
  s0: number,
  s1: number,
  o0: number,
  o1: number,
  y: number,
  color: Vec3,
): void {
  const at = (s: number, o: number): Vec3 => {
    const p = squarePathPoint(s);
    return [p.x + p.rx * o, y, p.z + p.rz * o];
  };
  pushQuad(out, [at(s0, o1), at(s1, o1), at(s1, o0), at(s0, o0)], color);
}
```

gap - carLength : null;\n    },\n    findSpawnSlot: (cars, carParams, params, carLength) => {\n      let best: { s: number; lane: number } | null = null;\n      let bestScore = -Infinity;\n      for (let lane = 0; lane <= 1; lane++) {\n        for (let k = 0; k < 32; k++) {\n          const s = (k * c) / 32;\n          let leaderGap = Infinity;\n          let leaderV = params.v0;\n          let followerGap = Infinity;\n          let followerV = params.v0;\n          let followerParams: IdmParams | null = null;\n          cars.forEach((car, j) => {\n            if (car.lane !== lane && car.laneProgress >= 1) return;\n            const fwd = (((car.s - s) % c) + c) % c;\n            if (fwd < leaderGap) {\n              leaderGap = fwd;\n              leaderV = car.v;\n            }\n            const back = (c - fwd) % c;\n            if (back < followerGap) {\n              followerGap = back;\n              followerV = car.v;\n              followerParams = carParams[j];\n            }\n          });\n          if (idmAcceleration(params.v0, leaderGap - carLength, params.v0 - leaderV, params) < -B_SAFE)\n            continue;\n          if (\n            followerParams !== null &&\n            idmAcceleration(followerV, followerGap - carLength, followerV - params.v0, followerParams) <\n              -B_SAFE\n          )\n            continue;\n          const score = Math.min(leaderGap, followerGap);\n          if (score > bestScore) {\n            bestScore = score;\n            best = { s, lane };\n          }\n        }\n      }\n      return best;\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nfunction ringScene(): SceneDef {\n  return {\n    c: RING_C,\n    obstacles: [{ s: STOP_S }],\n    lamps: [RING_LAMP],\n    buildStatic: ringStatic,\n    ...ringTopology(RING_C),\n    carPose(car) {",

function roadCarPose(road: Road, car: Car): Pose {
  const fromLane = road.lanes[Math.round(car.laneFrom)];
  const toLane = road.lanes[car.lane];
  const span = car.lane - car.laneFrom;
  const t = span === 0 ? 1 : (car.lateral - car.laneFrom) / span;
  const offset = fromLane.offset + (toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * t;
  const offsetVel = span === 0 ? 0 : ((toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * car.lateralVel) / span;
  const dir = toLane.direction;
  const p = road.point(car.s);
  const yaw = Math.atan2(offsetVel * dir, Math.max(car.v, 1));
  return {
    x: p.x + p.rx * offset,
    y: 0.02,
    z: p.z + p.rz * offset,
    angle: Math.atan2(-p.hz, p.hx) + (dir < 0 ? Math.PI : 0) + yaw,
    pitch: 0,
  };
}

Key insight from the existing code: the sim is 1D per lane with "virtual standing car" obstacles. The road end already acts as a stop sign. Connecting roads = replacing the end obstacle with "the first car on the next road" as a virtual leader, plus traffic-light-style right-of-way at the crossing point.

Let me think about the real design options:

**Option A: Endpoint connections (road graph).** Roads are edges; intersections are nodes that just link lane ends: exit lane of road A continues into entrance lane of road B. Cars cross the seam seamlessly: when a car's s exceeds road length, it moves to the next road (s -= length, road/lane mapping) OR (better for IDM) cars stay on their road but the leader lookup "sees through" the seam: distance to leader = (distance to my end) + (leader's s on next road). No traffic lights — this is for continuous flow (highway ramps, roundabouts). 

**Option B: Conflict-point intersection.** For a real 4-way crossing: the intersection is a conflict ZONE, not a road. Cars don't turn inside it initially — each approach lane maps to an exit road (path through the zone for rendering). Right-of-way: traffic light phases (NS green / EW green) implemented as the existing obstacle mechanism: a red phase puts a virtual standing car at the stop line of each approach in that direction. That's exactly the existing RED_LIGHT obstacle logic — it generalizes: instead of one obstacle per light, each intersection holds N approach stop lines, activated by phase.

The adaptive question: given roads with different lane counts/directions, how to build the intersection geometry and lane mapping automatically?

My suggestion, concretely:

1. **Intersection = connection table + conflict zone, computed from the roads' endpoint poses.** Each Road already exposes `point(s)` → position + heading + right normal. An intersection placed at a point gathers all road ends near it. Each approach (incoming direction) has lanes entering (toward intersection) and lanes leaving. The adaptive part:
   - Approach heading from `road.point(end).h` — the intersection figures out approach angles automatically.
   - Lane count/offsets from `road.lanes` — the approach width = f×4 + b×4, computed from config.
   - So the intersection geometry is derived: approach centerline = road end point, normal = road heading.

2. **Sim model (minimal viable): keep cars on roads; the intersection only supplies (a) through-mapping (which exit road/lane each entry lane feeds) and (b) a virtual obstacle at each stop line controlled by a phase.** The leader search extends across the seam: for a car near the end of road A, its "leader" may be the last car on the connected road B at distance (gapToEnd + leaderB.s). Implement by making stepRoad connection-aware: connections list {fromRoad, fromLane, toRoad, toLane}. Turning (choosing which exit) comes later; start with straight-through default mapping.

3. **Geometry: build the intersection box from approach extents.** The zone boundary on each approach = stop line position, placed at distance d from the center, where d = half the max crossing width (computed from perpendicular road widths + corner radius). The static mesh: fill the zone with asphalt polygon; approach roads are clipped at the stop lines. Lane guide lines (dashed) can be drawn through the zone as bezier arcs from entry lane offset to exit lane offset — also derived from the lane offset tables.

4. **Right of way: reuse the existing traffic-light obstacle system per intersection.** Each intersection gets a phase clock; approaches grouped into phases (e.g., the two opposing directions). Good instinct to pause here — this is the fork in the architecture. My suggestion: don't start with an `Intersection` class. Start with a smaller primitive, because "connect 2 roads" and "4-way crossing" are different problems wearing the same coat.

**The core mechanism (works for both): the seam as a virtual leader.** The sim already treats a road end as a virtual standing car. A connection just swaps that obstacle for a virtual *moving* car — the tail car of the next road. For a car at `s` near the end of road A (direction +1) connected to road B:

```
gap to leader on B = (L_A − s) + leaderB.s
closingSpeed     = v − leaderB.v
```

Feed that into the same `idmAcceleration` call and cars brake/cruise across the seam exactly like they follow on one road. When `s` crosses `L_A`, the car teleports to road B with `s -= L_A`, keeping `v`. Lane changes stay road-local. That's the whole trick — no intersection physics needed yet.

**Then, the data model:**

```ts
type RoadEnd = { road: Road; end: 'start' | 'end' };
type Connection = { from: RoadEnd; to: RoadEnd };
```

Each road end is either `stop` (current behavior) or a `Connection`. This is where "adaptive" lives, and it's derived entirely from what `Road` already knows:

- **Heading**: `road.point(0|L).h` gives each approach's direction — the connection builder can align/merge geometries automatically from poses, not hand-tuned coordinates.
- **Lane mapping**: entry lanes are lanes whose direction points *into* the seam; exit lanes point *away*. Map them by offset order — entry lane i → exit lane min(i, exits−1). A 2-lane-into-1-lane connection degrades into a natural merge, two-way into one-way works, no special-casing.

**Where Intersection earns its keep** — 3+ roads meeting, or conflicting flows. Then it's: approaches derived from the road ends near a point (heading + width from each road's lane config), a stop line per approach, and right-of-way implemented with your *existing* obstacle system: a phase clock, and red phase = virtual standing car at that approach's stop line. Geometry (zone size, guide curves from entry lane to exit lane) is all computed from the lane offset tables — nothing hand-placed.

Suggested build order:

1. **Connection primitive** — two roads end-to-end (straight or with a bend), seamless flow, proves the virtual-leader seam. Small, testable in the check file (car crosses without speed jump, no collision across the seam).
2. **Intersection class** — one 4-way, 2-phase light (reuse the light cycle GUI), approaches auto-derived.
3. **Turns** — per-car exit choice + guide paths through the zone. Genuinely harder; defer.

Placement algorithm in scenes.ts (scene3 build):
```ts
function buildScene3Roads(cfgA: RoadConfig, cfgB: RoadConfig) {
  const roadA = new Road(cfgA);
  const roadB = new Road(cfgB);
  const tA = identity transform;
  const end = roadA.point(roadA.length);
  const b0 = roadB.point(0);
  const phi = Math.atan2(end.hz, end.hx) - Math.atan2(b0.hz, b0.hx);
  const cos = Math.cos(phi), sin = Math.sin(phi);
  // rotate b0 position by phi, then translate so it lands at end.(x,z)
  const rx = b0.x * cos + b0.z * sin;
  const rz = -b0.x * sin + b0.z * cos;
  const tB = { tx: end.x - rx, tz: end.z - rz, cos, sin };
}
```

function applyTransform(p: PathPoint, t): PathPoint {
  return {
    x: p.x * t.cos + p.z * t.sin + t.tx,
    z: -p.x * t.sin + p.z * t.cos + t.tz,
    hx: p.hx * t.cos + p.hz * t.sin,
    hz: -p.hx * t.sin + p.hz * t.cos,
    rx: p.rx * t.cos + p.rz * t.sin,
    rz: -p.rx * t.sin + p.rz * t.cos,
  };
}
```

Network module design (sim/network.ts):

```ts
import { advanceLateral, B_SAFE, DELTA_A, idmAcceleration, LANE_CHANGE_COOLDOWN, type Car, type IdmParams } from './idm';
import type { Road } from './road';

/** A lane exit connected to another road's lane entrance. */
export interface LaneConnection {
  toRoad: number;
  toLane: number; // local lane index on the target road
  entranceS: number; // arc position where traffic enters the target road
}

export interface Network {
  roads: Road[];
  /** Global lane table: [road][localLane] → global lane index. */
  laneOffsets: number[];
  numLanes: number;
  /** exit[road][lane] = connection at the lane's exit end, or null for a stop. */
  exit: (LaneConnection | null)[][];
}

export function buildNetwork(roads: Road[], links: [number, number][]): Network {
  // links: pairs of road indices joined end→start
  const laneOffsets = ...prefix sums;
  const exit = roads.map(r => r.lanes.map(() => null));
  for (const [a, b] of links) {
    const roadA = roads[a], roadB = roads[b];
    // A forward lanes (exit at end) → B forward lanes (entrance at 0)
    const fwdA = indices of A lanes dir+1, fwdB = B dir+1;
    fwdA.forEach((lane, i) => exit[a][lane] = { toRoad: b, toLane: fwdB[Math.min(i, fwdB.length - 1)], entranceS: 0 });
    // B backward lanes (exit at start) → A backward lanes (entrance at L_A)
    const backA = A dir−1 indices, backB = B dir−1;
    backB.forEach((lane, j) => exit[b][lane] = { toRoad: a, toLane: backA[Math.min(j, backA.length - 1)], entranceS: roadA.length });
  }
}
```

function locate(net: Network, global: number): { road: number; lane: number } {
  // linear scan fine for tiny networks
  for (let r = net.roads.length - 1; r >= 0; r--) if (global >= net.laneOffsets[r]) return { road: r, lane: global - net.laneOffsets[r] };

  let accel = idmAcceleration(car.v, 1e6, 0, params[i]);
  // leader in the same lane (same road)
  let gap = Infinity, vLead = 0;
  for (let j = 0; j < cars.length; j++) {
    if (j === i || cars[j].lane !== car.lane) continue;
    const d = (cars[j].s - car.s) * dir;
    if (d > 0 && d < gap) { gap = d; vLead = cars[j].v; }

  // downstream: stop end or virtual leader across the seam
  const dEnd = dir > 0 ? road.length - car.s : car.s;
  const down = downstream(net, cars, i, ri, li, dEnd, carLength);
  accel = Math.min(accel, idmAcceleration(car.v, down.gap, car.v - down.vLead, params[i]));

```ts
export function buildScene3(cfgA: RoadConfig, cfgB: RoadConfig): { net: Network; transforms: Transform[] } {
  const roadA = new Road(cfgA);
  const roadB = new Road(cfgB);
  const net = buildNetwork([roadA, roadB], [[0, 1]]);
  const tA: Transform = { tx: 0, tz: 0, cos: 1, sin: 0 };
  const tB = placeAtEnd(roadA, roadB);
  return { net, transforms: [tA, tB] };
}

function placeAtEnd(roadA: Road, roadB: Road): Transform {
  const end = roadA.point(roadA.length);
  const b0 = roadB.point(0);
  const phi = Math.atan2(end.hz, end.hx) - Math.atan2(b0.hz, b0.hx);
  const cos = Math.cos(phi);
  const sin = Math.sin(phi);
  const rx = b0.x * cos + b0.z * sin;
  const rz = -b0.x * sin + b0.z * cos;
  return { tx: end.x - rx, tz: end.z - rz, cos, sin };
}
```

const from = locate(net, Math.round(car.laneFrom));
const to = locate(net, car.lane);
const road = net.roads[to.road];
const fromLane = road.lanes[from.lane]; // from/to same road during slides
const toLane = road.lanes[to.lane];
const span = car.lane - car.laneFrom;
const t2 = span === 0 ? 1 : (car.lateral - car.laneFrom) / span;
const offset = fromLane.offset + (toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * t2;
const offsetVel = span === 0 ? 0 : ((toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * car.lateralVel) / span;
const dir = toLane.direction;
const p = applyTransform(road.point(car.s), transforms[to.road]);
const yaw = Math.atan2(-offsetVel * dir, Math.max(car.v, 1));
return { x: p.x + p.rx * offset, y: 0.02, z: p.z + p.rz * offset, angle: Math.atan2(-p.hz, p.hx) + (dir < 0 ? Math.PI : 0) + yaw, pitch: 0 };

s < L; s += 2) {\n    pushPathPatch(verts, path, s, Math.min(s + 2, L), -0.075, 0.075, 0.03, yellow);\n  }\n\n  // White dashes between same-direction lanes.\n  const paint: Vec3 = [0.9, 0.9, 0.9];\n  const dashOffsets: number[] = [];\n  for (let i = 1; i < f; i++) dashOffsets.push(4 * i);\n  for (let j = 1; j < b; j++) dashOffsets.push(-4 * j);\n  for (const o of dashOffsets) {\n    for (let s = 0; s < L; s += 6) {\n      pushPathPatch(verts, path, s, Math.min(s + 2, L), o - 0.075, o + 0.075, 0.03, paint);\n    }\n  }\n\n  return verts;\n}\n\nfunction roadCarPose(road: Road, car: Car): Pose {\n  const fromLane = road.lanes[Math.round(car.laneFrom)];\n  const toLane = road.lanes[car.lane];\n  const span = car.lane - car.laneFrom;\n  const t = span === 0 ? 1 : (car.lateral - car.laneFrom) / span;\n  const offset = fromLane.offset + (toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * t;\n  const offsetVel = span === 0 ? 0 : ((toLane.offset - fromLane.offset) * car.lateralVel) / span;\n  const dir = toLane.direction;\n  const p = road.point(car.s);\n  // Nose along the true velocity: travel direction plus the lateral slide. nearestInLane returns { index, gap, v } — accelToward uses leader.gap − carLength and car.v − leader.vLead — vLead undefined → NaN!

Note: downstream's gap already has carLength subtracted (tail: −carLength; stop: −carLength/2). And in stepNetwork I call `idmAcceleration(car.v, down.gap, car.v - down.vLead, params[i])` directly (not via accelToward) ✓ that's consistent.

Done, checks and build green. Step 1 is working — two roads, one seam, seamless flow.

What got built:

- **`src/sim/network.ts`** — the connection primitive. `buildNetwork(roads, links)` derives lane connections automatically (A's forward lanes feed B's, B's backward lanes feed A's, clamped by index for mismatched counts). `stepNetwork` adds the *downstream constraint*: a car's brake target at its lane end is now the stop sign **or** the tail car on the connected road — walking the chain while lanes are empty, so a queue at the network's far end propagates upstream correctly. Seam crossing remaps the car to the next road's lane, keeping speed and overshoot.
- **Scene 3** is now Road A + Road B (separate GUI folders). B is auto-placed at A's end with heading continuity — default demo is a straight 150 m road into a 90° arc. Cars flow A → B around the bend; enable lanes back on both and opposing traffic flows B → A. Spawning only happens at the network's unfed entrances.
- `stepRoad` was deleted — the single-road checks now run on a one-road network with identical behavior.

New checks prove the seam: crossing at full speed (~12 m/s, no dip), a stop at the far end backing cars up across the seam without collision (final bumper gap > 0), and a backward-lane car crossing B → A. Credit to `tsc`: it caught a `vLead`/`v` field mixup that would've been silent NaN accelerations at runtime.

One honest limitation: the stop sign at the very end of the chain brakes cars IDM-hard if they arrive fast (the ~248 m desired gap to a standing obstacle at 30 m/s). Real drivers would coast in; that needs the "anticipation" layer whenever you want it. Next per the plan: the `Intersection` class (step 2) whenever you're ready.

Yes — step 2, the 4-way intersection. Scope for this pass: straight-through traffic only (turns are step 3), 2-phase signal with all-red clearance, approaches auto-derived from road configs. The design that keeps it small:

- The crossing is just **two short connector roads** (NS and EW) inside the zone, linked to 4 approach roads with the existing seam machinery — cars flow through the box exactly like across any seam.
- The signal is the existing obstacle trick, per direction group: entries of the stopped direction get a virtual standing car at their stop line. Phase machine: NS green → NS yellow → all-red → EW green → EW yellow → all-red.
- `SceneDef` gets phase-driven contracts (`phaseAt` / `obstaclesFor` / `lampColor`) so scenes 1–2 and the intersection share the renderer.

Four approach roads (S/N/E/W) meet two short connector roads (NS and\n * EW) inside the zone; links wire them end-to-start so cars flow straight through.\n * Right-of-way is a 2-phase signal with an all-red clearance: the stopped direction's\n * entries get a virtual standing car at their stop line.\n *\n * Road order in the network: [S, N, E, W, NS connector, EW connector].\n */\nimport { buildNetwork, globalLane, type NetObstacle, type Network } from './network';\nimport { Road } from './road';\n\nexport interface IntersectionConfig {\n  approach: number; // m, length of each approach road\n  lanesEachWay: number; // lanes per direction on every approach\n}\n\nexport interface IntersectionState {\n  net: Network;\n  zoneHalf: number; // half the zone's side length (m)\n  /** Stop-line obstacles per direction group (global lane + s). */\n  entries: { ns: NetObstacle[]; ew: NetObstacle[] };\n  /** Road indices. */\n  idx: { s: number; n: number; e: number; w: number; nsConn: number; ewConn: number };\n}\n\nexport const IDX = { s: 0, n: 1, e: 2, w: 3, nsConn: 4, ewConn: 5 } as const;\n\nexport function buildIntersection(cfg: IntersectionConfig): IntersectionState {\n  const lanes = cfg.lanesEachWay;\n  const mk = (length: number): Road =>\n    new Road({\n      shape: 'straight',\n      length,\n      radius: 50,\n      angle: 90,\n      lanesForward: lanes,\n      lanesBackward: lanes,\n    });\n\n  const zoneHalf = (8 * lanes) / 2 + 2; // road width + 2 m margin each side\n  const approach = mk(cfg.approach);\n  const nsConn = mk(zoneHalf * 2);\n  const ewConn = mk(zoneHalf * 2);\n  const roads = [approach, approach, approach, approach, nsConn, ewConn].map(\n    (r) => new Road(r.config),\n  );\n  const net = buildNetwork(roads, [\n    [IDX.s, IDX.nsConn],\n    [IDX.nsConn, IDX.n],\n    [IDX.w, IDX.ewConn],\n    [IDX.ewConn, IDX.e],\n  ]);\n\n  // Signalized entries: lanes whose travel exits into the zone.\n  const ns: NetObstacle[] = [];\n  const ew: NetObstacle[] = [];\n  roads[IDX.s].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction > 0) ns.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.s, li), s: cfg.approach });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.n].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction < 0) ns.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.n, li), s: 0 });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.w].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction > 0) ew.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.w, li), s: cfg.approach });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.e].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction < 0) ew.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.e, li), s: 0 });\n  });\n\n  return { net, zoneHalf, entries: { ns, ew }, idx: IDX };\n}\n\nexport type IntersectionPhase = 'nsGreen' | 'nsYellow' | 'ewGreen' | 'ewYellow' | 'allRed';\n\nexport interface SignalSettings {\n  green: number;\n  yellow: number;\n  red: number;\n  override: string;\n}\n\n/** 2-phase cycle with all-red clearance: nsGreen → nsYellow → allRed → ewGreen → ewYellow → allRed. */\nexport function intersectionPhaseAt(clock: number, light: SignalSettings): IntersectionPhase {\n  if (light.override === 'green') return 'nsGreen';\n  if (light.override === 'yellow') return 'nsYellow';\n  if (light.override === 'red') return 'allRed';\n  const { green: g, yellow: y, red: r } = light;\n  const t = clock % (2 * (g + y + r));\n  if (t < g) return 'nsGreen';\n  if (t < g + y) return 'nsYellow';\n  if (t < g + y + r) return 'allRed';\n  if (t < 2 * g + y + r) return 'ewGreen';\n  if (t < 2 * g + 2 * y + r) return 'ewYellow';\n  return 'allRed';\n}\n\n/** Obstacles {\n    case 'nsGreen':\n      return state.entries.ew;\n    case 'ewGreen':\n      return state.entries.ns;\n    default:\n      return [...state.entries.ns, ...state.entries.ew]; // yellow transitions and all-red: full stop\n  }\n}\n\n/** What one lamp stack shows. 'green' : 'red';\n    case 'nsYellow':\n      return nsGroup ? 'yellow' : 'red';\n    case 'ewGreen':\n      return nsGroup ? 'red' : 'green';\n    case 'ewYellow':\n      return nsGroup ? export const scene4State: { state: IntersectionState | null; transforms: Transform[] } = { state: null, transforms: [] };

function placeAt(road: Road, atS: number, target: { x: number; z: number; hx: number; hz: number }): Transform {
  const p = road.point(atS);
  const phi = Math.atan2(target.hz, target.hx) - Math.atan2(p.hz, p.hx);
  const cos = Math.cos(phi);
  const sin = Math.sin(phi);
  return { tx: target.x - (p.x * cos + p.z * sin), tz: target.z - (-p.x * sin + p.z * cos), cos, sin };
}

export function buildScene4(cfg: IntersectionConfig): void {
  const state = buildIntersection(cfg);
  const zh = state.zoneHalf;
  const L = cfg.approach;
  const conn = state.net.roads[IDX.nsConn];

  scene4State.transforms = [
    placeAt(state.net.roads[IDX.s], L, { x: 0, z: -zh, hx: 0, hz: 1 }),
    placeAt(state.net.roads[IDX.n], 0, { x: 0, z: zh, hx: 0, hz: 1 }),
    placeAt(state.net.roads[IDX.e], 0, { x: zh, z: 0, hx: 1, hz: 0 }),

    placeAt(state.net.roads[IDX.ewConn], 0, { x: -zh, z: 0, hx: 1, hz: 0 }),
  ];
}

Done, checks and build green. **Scene 4 (intersection)** is live — and the "adaptively create the intersection" question from before is now answered in code: the whole thing is derived from `IntersectionConfig { approach, lanesEachWay }`.

How it's put together:

- **`src/sim/intersection.ts`**: 4 approach roads + 2 connector roads (NS/EW) inside the zone, wired by 4 end→start links — the seam machinery carries cars straight through the box. Entries are auto-tagged into NS/EW groups from lane directions; the zone size comes from lane count.
- **Signal**: 2-phase cycle (NS green → NS yellow → all-red → EW green → EW yellow → all-red) using your existing green/yellow/red durations; red duration is now the all-red clearance. The stopped direction's entries get virtual standing cars at their stop lines. Override maps to: green = NS, red = all-stop, yellow = NS yellow.
- **Scene**: 4 lamp stacks on the right of each entering approach (correct red/yellow/green per group), stop lines, zebras at all 4 crossings, day/night, orbit, add/delete cars — spawn points are the 4 outer entrances, so traffic flows in from every side.
- **Checks**: phase-cycle order, nsGreen crossing at speed, all-red full stop at the line, and the important one — conflict safety: while NS flows, the W car is held at its line (no zone collision).

Honest limitations for next time: straight-through only (no turns — that's step 3, needs per-car exit choice and guide paths through the zone), and pedestrians are still just paint. The `Intersection` is scene-4-shaped but the sim half is reusable: `buildIntersection` + phase machine + entry groups are exactly what a scene of *multiple* connected intersections would call.

Phase machine rework:
```ts
export function intersectionPhaseAt(clock: number, light: SignalSettings): IntersectionPhase {
  if (light.override === 'green') return 'nsGreen';
  if (light.override === 'yellow') return 'nsYellow';
  if (light.override === 'red') return 'allRed';
  const { green: g, yellow: y } = light;
  const t = clock % (2 * (g + y));
  if (t < g) return 'nsGreen';
  if (t < g + y) return 'nsYellow';
  if (t < 2 * g + y) return 'ewGreen';
  return 'ewYellow';
}
```
Period 2(g+y): [0,g) nsGreen; [g, g+y) nsYellow; [g+y, 2g+y) ewGreen; [2g+y, 2g+2y) ewYellow ✓ complementary ✓ (except override allRed).

**Current model**: The intersection is straight-through: S→NSc→N etc. Cars on the S approach forward lanes always go straight (connections fixed: S.forward[i] → NSc.forward[i] → N.forward[i]).

**What turns mean physically:**
- S approach, right turn (US driving, right-hand traffic): S (heading +z/north) turns right → heads −x? Right of +z heading: right = (−hz, hx) = (−1, 0) → −x = west. So S right turn → W road (exit westward).
- S left turn → E road (heading +x/east).
- Left turn yields to oncoming traffic: oncoming = N→S traffic (N backward lanes heading south). The left-turning car waits at the stop line until no opposing car is within some distance/time gap.

**How to implement in the network model:**

Each turning movement is a different connection from the approach to a different exit. Currently `exit[lane]` is a single LaneConnection (or null). For turns, an approach lane needs MULTIPLE possible exits: straight, right, left. The car CHOOSES one (route decision), then follows that connection.

Minimal model:
1. **Routes**: per approach lane, 3 possible connections: straight (S→N), right (S→W), left (S→E). Each is a connection through a connector path in the zone. The straight uses the existing NS connector. Right/left need connector paths: S→W is a right turn (short arc); S→E is a left turn (bigger arc crossing the center).

computeYieldObstacles in sim/intersection.ts:
```ts
export function leftTurnYieldObstacles(state: IntersectionState, cars: Car[], carLength: number): NetObstacle[] {
  const out: NetObstacle[] = [];
  cars.forEach((car, i) => {
    if (car.route !== ROUTE_LEFT) return;
    const { road, lane } = locate(state.net, car.lane);
    const entry = signalEntryFor(state, road, lane); // {lane, s} | undefined — only approach lanes have left routes
    if (!entry) return; // not on an approach lane (e.g., already in the zone): no yield
    // opposing traffic approaching the zone?
    const opposing = state.opposing[car.lane] ?? [];
    for (const lane of opposing) { if (any car within 45 of exit && v > 1) { out.push(entry); break; } }
  });
  return out;
}
```

```ts
if (this.scene === 3 || this.scene === 4) this.recycleCars();
private recycleCars(): void {
  this.cars.forEach((car, i) => {
    const { road: ri, lane: li } = locate(net, car.lane); // needs net! scene3State.net / scene4State.state.net
    const road = net.roads[ri];
    const dir = road.lanes[li].direction;
    const distToEnd = dir > 0 ? road.length - car.s : car.s;
    const hasExit = net.exit[ri][li].length > 0;
    if (!hasExit && distToEnd < 3 && car.v < 0.5) {
      const slot = this.def.findSpawnSlot(this.cars, this.carParams, this.carParams[i], this.gui.settings.carLength);
      if (slot) {
        car.s = slot.s; car.lane = slot.lane; car.lateral = slot.lane; car.laneFrom = slot.lane; car.laneProgress = 1; car.lateralVel = 0;
        car.v = this.carParams[i].v0; car.a = 0; car.cooldown = 0;
        car.route = this.scene === 4 ? randomRoute() : 0;
      }
    }
  });
}
```

This is step 3 (turns) — and it earns a real design before code. Here's the model I'll build:

- **Turn paths are real arc roads** (radius 2 m for right turns, 6 m for left, derived from lane offsets), linked into the network: `S.end → arc → W/E`. Every approach lane gets a connection *list* `[straight, right, left]`, and each car carries a `route` (60/20/20 random at spawn) selecting its exit. Seam machinery then handles turns for free — pose, downstream, crossing.
- **Left yield**: before each step, the intersection computes yield obstacles: a left-routed car on an approach gets a virtual stop at its stop line whenever an opposing-stream car is approaching the zone (<45 m, moving). Right turns flow freely on green.
- **Arc placement is pinned by entry pose** (`placeAt`), which also forced me to verify exit geometry against lane offsets.
- Bonus needed for watchability: cars reaching the network's dead ends now **recycle** to a safe entrance (same params, new route), or the scene jams after 30 s.

New link semantics: `[a, b, aEnd=1, bEnd=0]` where end 1 = road end (s=L), 0 = start (s=0). Lanes exiting at a-side feed lanes entering at b-side:
- exiting at end: forward lanes (dir+1); exiting at start: backward lanes (dir−1).
- entering at end: backward lanes (their travel starts at s=L); entering at start: forward lanes (travel starts at s=0).
Symmetric reverse: lanes exiting at b-side (per bEnd) feed lanes entering at a-side (per aEnd).

So the symmetric mapping: exiting lanes at each side feed entering lanes at the other side:
- exitA = lanes with direction matching aEnd (dir+1 if aEnd=1, dir−1 if aEnd=0)
- enterB = lanes with direction matching !bEnd... entering at bEnd: forward if bEnd=0, backward if bEnd=1.
Mapping exitA[i] → enterB[min(i, len−1)] with entranceS = bEnd===0 ? 0 : L_b.
And reverse: exitB[j] → enterA[min(j, ...)] with entranceS = aEnd===0 ? 0 : L_a.

```ts
export type RouteIndex = 0 | 1 | 2;
export const ROUTE_STRAIGHT = 0;
export const ROUTE_RIGHT = 1;
export const ROUTE_LEFT = 2;

export interface Network {
  roads: Road[];
  laneOffsets: number[];
  numLanes: number;
  /** exit[road][lane] = route-indexed connections at that lane's travel end ([] = stop). */
  exit: LaneConnection[][][];
}

/** A link between two road ends. end: 1 = road end (s = length), 0 = road start (s = 0). */
export type RoadLink = [a: number, b: number, aEnd?: number, bEnd?: number];

export function buildNetwork(roads: Road[], links: RoadLink[]): Network {
  const laneOffsets: number[] = [];
  let total = 0;
  for (const road of roads) { laneOffsets.push(total); total += road.lanes.length; }
  const exit: LaneConnection[][][] = roads.map((r) => r.lanes.map(() => []));

  const lanesAt = (roadIdx: number, end: number, exiting: boolean): number[] => {
    const dir = exiting ? (end === 1 ? 1 : -1) : end === 1 ? -1 : 1;
    return roads[roadIdx].lanes.flatMap((lane, i) => (lane.direction === dir ? [i] : []));
  };

  for (const [a, b, aEnd = 1, bEnd = 0] of links) {
    const exitA = lanesAt(a, aEnd, true);
    const enterB = lanesAt(b, bEnd, false);
    const exitB = lanesAt(b, bEnd, true);
    const enterA = lanesAt(a, aEnd, false);
    exitA.forEach((lane, i) => {
      exit[a][lane].push({ toRoad: b, toLane: enterB[Math.min(i, enterB.length - 1)], entranceS: bEnd === 0 ? 0 : roads[b].length });
    });
    exitB.forEach((lane, j) => {
      exit[b][lane].push({ toRoad: a, toLane: enterA[Math.min(j, enterA.length - 1)], entranceS: aEnd === 0 ? 0 : roads[a].length });
    });
  }
  return { roads, laneOffsets, numLanes: total, exit };
}
```

Entering at side: enter at end=1: backward lanes (they start travel at s=L, going to 0) ✓ dir=−1 ✓; at start: forward ✓ dir=+1 ✓.

Edge: enterB empty (e.g., connecting to a road with no lanes of that direction) — Math.min(i, -1) = -1 → toLane -1 broken! Guard: skip link direction if enterB empty? If no entering lanes, traffic has nowhere — treat as stop (no connection pushed): `if (enterB.length === 0) return;` per side. Add guards.

/** The connection a car follows at its lane's end, by route (clamped to what exists). */
function connectionFor(net: Network, road: number, lane: number, route: number): LaneConnection | null {
  const conns = net.exit[road][lane];
  if (conns.length === 0) return null;
  return conns[Math.min(route, conns.length - 1)];
}

```ts
const YIELD_DIST = 45; // m: opposing traffic closer than this to the zone blocks a left turn
const YIELD_MIN_SPEED = 1; // m/s: stopped opponents don't block

export function leftTurnYieldObstacles(state: IntersectionState, cars: Car[]): NetObstacle[] {
  const out: NetObstacle[] = [];
  const entryByLane = new Map<number, number>();
  [...state.entries.ns, ...state.entries.ew].forEach((e) => entryByLane.set(e.lane, e.s));
  cars.forEach((car, i) => {
    if (car.route !== ROUTE_LEFT) return;
    const s = entryByLane.get(car.lane);
    if (s === undefined) return; // not on an approach lane: no yield inside the zone
    const { road: ri } = locate(state.net, car.lane);
    const road = state.net.roads[ri];
    const dir = road.lanes[locate(state.net, car.lane).lane].direction;
    const distToLine = (s - car.s) * dir;
    if (distToLine < 0 || distToLine > YIELD_DIST) return; // already past the line or far away
    const blocked = (state.opposing.get(car.lane) ?? []).some((lane) =>
      cars.some((other, j) => {
        if (j === i || other.lane !== lane || other.v < YIELD_MIN_SPEED) return false;
        const d = ...dist of other to ITS lane end...;
        return d < YIELD_DIST;
      }),
    );
    if (blocked) out.push({ lane: car.lane, s });
  });
  return out;
}
```
opposing car's distance to its lane end: need its road/dir: locate + compute: d = dir > 0 ? L − s : s.

Hmm — yield obstacle: { lane: car.lane, s } — the car brakes for a standing obstacle at the stop line ✓ same as red. When opposing clears (passes through), blocked=false → proceeds ✓.

Edge: opponent in the ZONE on connector (their distToExit < 45 ✓ since connector is 8 m) ✓ blocked ✓. Opponent stopped at their red (v < 1) → not blocking ✓ left can go (realistic-ish).

Also export a helper for the renderer? scenes def.step will call leftTurnYieldObstacles.

Write the new intersection.ts pieces. Also keep intersectionObstacles/phaseAt/lampColor.

</details>

```ts
const YIELD_DIST = 45; // m: opposing traffic closer than this to the zone blocks a left turn
const YIELD_MIN_SPEED = 1; // m/s: stopped opponents don't block

/**
 * Stop-line obstacles for left-turning cars that must give way: a left-routed car on
 * an approach is held at its stop line while an opposing-stream car is approaching
 * the zone (and actually moving).
 */
export function leftTurnYieldObstacles(state: IntersectionState, cars: Car[]): NetObstacle[] {
  const out: NetObstacle[] = [];
  cars.forEach((car, i) => {
    if (car.route !== ROUTE_LEFT) return;
    const entry = [...state.entries.ns, ...state.entries.ew].find((e) => e.lane === car.lane);
    if (!entry) return; // not on an approach lane: no yield inside the zone
    const { road: ri } = locate(state.net, car.lane);
    const road = state.net.roads[ri];
    const dir = road.lanes[locate(state.net, car.lane).lane].direction;
    const distToLine = (entry.s - car.s) * dir;
    if (distToLine < 0) return; // already past the line
    const blocked = (state.opposing.get(car.lane) ?? []).some((lane) =>
      cars.some((other, j) => {
        if (j === i || other.lane !== lane || other.v < YIELD_MIN_SPEED) return false;
        const ol = locate(state.net, lane);
        const oDir = state.net.roads[ol.road].lanes[ol.lane].direction;
        const dist = oDir > 0 ? state.net.roads[ol.road].length - other.s : other.s;
        return dist < YIELD_DIST;
      }),
    );
    if (blocked) out.push(entry);
  });
  return out;
}
```
Optimization: locate per car per lane — tiny N, fine.

/** What one lamp stack shows. Lamp order: [S, N, E, W] — S/N are the NS group, E/W the EW group. */
export function intersectionLampColor(
  _state: IntersectionState,
  lamp: number,
  phase: IntersectionPhase,
): 'red' | 'yellow' | 'green' {
  const nsGroup = lamp < 2;
  switch (phase) {
    case 'nsGreen':
      return nsGroup ? 'green' : 'red';
    case 'nsYellow':
      return nsGroup ? 'yellow' : 'red';
    case 'ewGreen':
      return nsGroup ? 'red' : 'green';
    case 'ewYellow':
      return nsGroup ? 'red' : 'yellow';
    default:
      return 'red';
  }
}

```ts
  /** Cars stopped at an unconnected end "left the map": respawn them at a safe entrance. */
  private recycleCars(): void {
    const net = this.scene === 3 ? scene3State.net : this.scene === 4 ? (scene4State.state?.net ?? null) : null;
    if (!net) return;
    this.cars.forEach((car, i) => {
      const { road: ri, lane: li } = locate(net, car.lane);
      if (net.exit[ri][li].length > 0) return; // connected end: keeps flowing
      const road = net.roads[ri];
      const dir = road.lanes[li].direction;
      const distToEnd = dir > 0 ? road.length - car.s : car.s;
      if (distToEnd > 3 || car.v > 0.5) return;
      const slot = this.def.findSpawnSlot(this.cars, this.carParams, this.carParams[i], this.gui.settings.carLength);
      if (!slot) return;
      car.s = slot.s;
      car.lane = slot.lane;
      car.lateral = slot.lane;
      car.laneFrom = slot.lane;
      car.laneProgress = 1;
      car.lateralVel = 0;
      car.v = this.carParams[i].v0;
      car.a = 0;
      car.cooldown = 0;
      car.route = this.scene === 4 ? randomRoute() : 0;
    });
  }
```

Got it — this screenshot makes it obvious. Two things are wrong, and they're the same root cause:

1. **Every turn exits to the wrong side** (mirrored). My `r = (−hz, hx)` "right normal" is actually the **left** normal — so the whole road model has been left-hand traffic all along (invisible until turns). Turn exits got mirrored: S-right currently goes to W when a right turn from the south approach should go to E.
2. **The arcs bulge outside the zone** because their sweep centers sit on the mirrored side, so the drawn paths can't geometrically reach the exits they topologically link to. The checks passed because they verify topology (links), not geometry — lesson learned.

The fix: flip to right-hand traffic (`r = (hz, −hx)`), correct the exit table, re-place arc entries and lamps, and add a geometry check that verifies each arc's *end pose* actually lands on its exit lane — that class of bug can't hide again.

```ts
function randomRoute(available: number[]): number {
  // weighted: straight 60%, others split 40%
  if (available.length === 0) return 0;
  const straight = available.includes(0);
  const turns = available.filter((r) => r !== 0);
  const r = Math.random();
  if (straight && r < 0.6) return 0;
  if (turns.length > 0) return turns[Math.floor(Math.random() * turns.length)];
  return available[Math.floor(Math.random() * available.length)];
}
```

buildIntersection(cfg, handed):
```ts
const closed = cfg.closed;
const ways = { s: !closed.s, n: !closed.n, e: !closed.e, w: !closed.w };
const roadList: { key: string; road: Road }[] = [];
const add = (key: string, road: Road): number => roadList.push({ key, road }) - 1;
const idx: Record<string, number> = {};
if (ways.s) idx.s = add('s', mk(cfg.approach));
if (ways.n) idx.n = add('n', mk(cfg.approach));
if (ways.e) idx.e = add('e', mk(cfg.approach));
if (ways.w) idx.w = add('w', mk(cfg.approach));
// connectors when both endpoints open
if (ways.s && ways.n) idx.nsConn = add('nsConn', mk(zoneHalf * 2));
if (ways.e && ways.w) idx.ewConn = add('ewConn', mk(zoneHalf * 2));
// turn arcs per available movement
const movements = [
  { key: 'sRight', from: 's', to: 'w', r: rRight, angle: 90 },
  { key: 'sLeft', from: 's', to: 'e', r: rLeft, angle: -90 },
  { key: 'nRight', from: 'n', to: 'e', r: rRight, angle: 90 },
  { key: 'nLeft', from: 'n', to: 'w', r: rLeft, angle: -90 },
  { key: 'eRight', from: 'e', to: 's', r: rRight, angle: 90 },
  { key: 'eLeft', from: 'e', to: 'n', r: rLeft, angle: -90 },
  { key: 'wRight', from: 'w', to: 'n', r: rRight, angle: 90 },
  { key: 'wLeft', from: 'w', to: 's', r: rLeft, angle: -90 },
];
for (const m of movements) if (ways[m.from] && ways[m.to]) idx[m.key] = add(m.key, mkArc(m.r, m.angle));
```

Good feature — and it forces the scene-4 construction to be properly data-driven. Design:

- `closed: { n, e, s, w }` in the intersection config (4 checkboxes: N=top/A, E=right/B, S=bottom/C, W=left/D).
- **Closed ways are never built**: no approach road, no ribbon, no stop line, no lamp, no spawns. Straight connectors are dropped when either endpoint is closed, turn arcs dropped when source or exit is closed.
- **Routes respect closures**: connection list entries for closed exits become `null`; spawn/recycle picks a route only among what actually exists (so on a T with N closed, S traffic only ever turns; on an L corner, traffic flows purely through the surviving turns).
- Yield degrades correctly for free (no opposing stream → left turns flow).
- Road indices become key-based (`'s'`, `'nRight'`, …) since slots are no longer fixed.

```ts
export type WayState = 'open' | 'in' | 'out' | 'both';

export interface IntersectionConfig {
  approach: number;
  lanesEachWay: number;
  closed: { n: WayState; e: WayState; s: WayState; w: WayState };
}

export function buildIntersection(cfg: IntersectionConfig, handed = 1): IntersectionState {
  const lanes = cfg.lanesEachWay;
  const zoneHalf = 4 * lanes;
  const stateOf = cfg.closed;
  const built = (k: 'n'|'e'|'s'|'w') => stateOf[k] !== 'both';
  const canEnter = (k) => stateOf[k] === 'open' || stateOf[k] === 'out';
  const canExit = (k) => stateOf[k] === 'open' || stateOf[k] === 'in';

  const roadIndex: Record<string, number> = {};
  const roads: Road[] = [];
  const add = (key: string, road: Road): number => { roadIndex[key] = roads.length; roads.push(road); return roadIndex[key]; };
  if (built('s')) add('s', mk(cfg.approach));
  if (built('n')) add('n', mk(cfg.approach));
  if (built('e')) add('e', mk(cfg.approach));
  if (built('w')) add('w', mk(cfg.approach));
  // connectors: each flow direction independently possible; build if any flow uses it
  const nsFlow = (canEnter('s') && canExit('n')) || (canEnter('n') && canExit('s'));
  const ewFlow = (canEnter('w') && canExit('e')) || (canEnter('e') && canExit('w'));
  if (nsFlow) add('nsConn', mk(zoneHalf * 2));
  if (ewFlow) add('ewConn', mk(zoneHalf * 2));
  // turn arcs: from needs canEnter, to needs canExit
  const moves: [string, string, string, number, number][] = [
    ['sRight', 's', 'w', rRight, 90],
    ['sLeft', 's', 'e', rLeft, -90],
    ['nRight', 'n', 'e', rRight, 90],
    ['nLeft', 'n', 'w', rLeft, -90],
    ['eRight', 'e', 's', rRight, 90],
    ['eLeft', 'e', 'n', rLeft, -90],
    ['wRight', 'w', 'n', rRight, 90],
    ['wLeft', 'w', 's', rLeft, -90],
  ];
  for (const [key, from, to, r, angle] of moves) {
    if (canEnter(from as Way) && canExit(to as Way)) add(key, mkArc(r, angle));
  }

  const links: RoadLink[] = [];
  const has = (k: string) => roadIndex[k] !== undefined;
  if (has('s') && has('nsConn')) links.push([roadIndex.s, roadIndex.nsConn]);
  if (has('nsConn') && has('n')) links.push([roadIndex.nsConn, roadIndex.n]);
  if (has('w') && has('ewConn')) links.push([roadIndex.w, roadIndex.ewConn]);
  if (has('ewConn') && has('e')) links.push([roadIndex.ewConn, roadIndex.e]);
  const entryFlag = (k: string) => (k === 'n' || k === 'e' ? 0 : 1); // N/E enter from their start side
  for (const [key, from] of moves.map((m) => [m[0], m[1]] as const)) {
    if (has(key) && has(from)) links.push([roadIndex[from], roadIndex[key], entryFlag(from), 0] as RoadLink);
  }
  const exitLinks: Record<string, RoadLink> = {
    sRight: [roadIndex.sRight, roadIndex.w, 1, 1],
    sLeft: [roadIndex.sLeft, roadIndex.e],
    nRight: [roadIndex.nRight, roadIndex.e],
    nLeft: [roadIndex.nLeft, roadIndex.w, 1, 1],
    eRight: [roadIndex.eRight, roadIndex.s, 1, 1],
    eLeft: [roadIndex.eLeft, roadIndex.n],
    wRight: [roadIndex.wRight, roadIndex.n],
    wLeft: [roadIndex.wLeft, roadIndex.s, 1, 1],
  };
  for (const [key, to] of moves.map((m) => [m[0], m[2]] as const)) {
    if (has(key) && has(to)) links.push(exitLinks[key]);
  }

  const net = buildNetwork(roads, links);
  
  // entryFlag for approach→arc: S/W enter zone at road END (end=1), N/E at road START (end=0) — the aEnd side. My entryFlag returns the aEnd: for [from, arc, aEnd, bEnd=0]: N/E → aEnd = 0 ✓ (matches earlier [IDX.n, ARC, 0, 0]).

  // Post-process closures:
  const closedLanes = new Set<number>();
  // exit-closed ways: remove all connections targeting that road
  for (const way of ['s', 'n', 'e', 'w'] as const) {
    if (!canExit(way) && has(way)) {
      net.exit.forEach((roadExits) =>
        roadExits.forEach((conns) => {
          conns.forEach((conn, i) => {
            if (conn && conn.toRoad === roadIndex[way]) conns[i] = null;
          });
        }),
      );
    }
    if (!canEnter(way) && has(way)) {
      // entering lanes of this approach: no connection out, no spawns
      net.roads[roadIndex[way]].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {
        const entering = lane.direction === enteringDir(way);
        if (entering) {
          net.exit[roadIndex[way]][li] = [];
          closedLanes.add(globalLane(net, roadIndex[way], li));
        }
      });
    }
  }
  net.closedLanes = closedLanes;

  // route lists per approach lane (straight/right/left by availability)
  ...for each open approach road: for each lane with conns.length: straight = conns[0] ?? null; right = arc exists ? {toRoad: arc} : null; left = ...; assign [straight, right, left] per lane type (outer/inner)...

  // entries (signals) only for canEnter ways; opposing for lanes of canEnter ways whose opposing stream exists.
```

Yes, that makes complete sense — it's the real-world distinction between "Do Not Enter", "No Exit", and "road closed":

- **Entry closed**: the approach's entering lanes can't flow into the zone (no signal link, no spawns there, stop sign at the edge for anything already on them) — but traffic can still *exit* toward it.
- **Exit closed**: connections into that road are removed — cars can enter from it but nothing returns.
- **Fully closed**: the road isn't built at all (the T / L cases).

Model: each way gets a 4-state dropdown (`open / in / out / both`), and the intersection builder goes key-based and conditional: roads, connectors (built when *either* direction of flow exists), turn arcs (source needs entry-open, target needs exit-open), signal entries, lamps, spawn filtering, and route availability all derive from the three predicates. This replaces the all-or-nothing design I was mid-build on — better requirement, same machinery.

184	export type IntersectionPhase = 'nsGreen' | 'nsYellow' | 'ewGreen' | 'ewYellow' | 'allRed';

186	export interface SignalSettings {
187	  green: number;
188	  yellow: number;
189	  red: number;

193	/** Complementary 2-phase cycle: nsGreen → nsYellow → ewGreen → ewYellow. One pair is always
194	 * green or yellow while the other is red — they are never red together (except the manual
195	 * all-red override). The red slider is unused here: each pair's red is the other's green. */
196	export function intersectionPhaseAt(clock: number, light: SignalSettings): IntersectionPhase {
197	  if (light.override === 'green') return 'nsGreen';
198	  if (light.override === 'yellow') return 'nsYellow';
199	  if (light.override === 'red') return 'allRed';
200	  const { green: g, yellow: y } = light;
201	  const t = clock % (2 * (g + y));
202	  if (t < g) return 'nsGreen';
203	  if (t < g + y) return 'nsYellow';
204	  if (t < 2 * g + y) return 'ewGreen';
205	  return 'ewYellow';
206	}
207	
208	/** Obstacles to enforce for a phase: the stopped direction(s) get their stop lines. */
209	export function intersectionObstacles(state: IntersectionState, phase: IntersectionPhase): NetObstacle[] {
210	  switch (phase) {
211	    case 'nsGreen':
212	      return state.entries.ew;
213	    case 'ewGreen':
214	      return state.entries.ns;
215	    default:
216	      return [...state.entries.ns, ...state.entries.ew]; // yellow transitions and all-red: full stop
217	  }

other lanes straight-only.\n  const approaches: { road: number; rightArc: number; leftArc: number }[] = [\n    { road: IDX.s, rightArc: ARC.sRight, leftArc: ARC.sLeft },\n    { road: IDX.n, rightArc: ARC.nRight, leftArc: ARC.nLeft },\n    { road: IDX.e, rightArc: ARC.eRight, leftArc: ARC.eLeft },\n    { road: IDX.w, rightArc: ARC.wRight, leftArc: ARC.wLeft },\n  ];\n  for (const { road: r, rightArc, leftArc } of approaches) {\n    net.roads[r].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n      const conns = net.exit[r][li];\n      if (conns.length === 0) return; // lanes leaving the zone, not entering it\n      const straight = conns[0];\n      const right: LaneConnection = { toRoad: rightArc, toLane: 0, entranceS: 0 };\n      const left: LaneConnection = { toRoad: leftArc, toLane: 0, entranceS: 0 };\n      const forwardOuter = lane.direction > 0 && li === lanes - 1;\n      const forwardInner = lane.direction > 0 && li === 0;\n      const backwardOuter = lane.direction < 0 && li === net.roads[r].lanes.length - 1;\n      const backwardInner = lane.direction < 0 && li === lanes;\n      conns[ROUTE_RIGHT] = forwardOuter || backwardOuter ? right : straight;\n      conns[ROUTE_LEFT] = forwardInner || backwardInner ? left : straight;\n      conns[ROUTE_STRAIGHT] = straight;\n    });\n  }\n\n  // Signalized entries: lanes whose travel exits into the zone, stopping at their stop\n  // line (set back from the zone edge so the crosswalk fits after it).\n  const ns: NetObstacle[] = [];\n  const ew: NetObstacle[] = [];\n  roads[IDX.s].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction > 0) ns.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.s, li), s: cfg.approach - STOP_BACK });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.n].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction < 0) ns.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.n, li), s: STOP_BACK });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.w].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction > 0) ew.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.w, li), s: cfg.approach - STOP_BACK });\n  });\n  roads[IDX.e].lanes.forEach((lane, li) => {\n    if (lane.direction < 0) ew.push({ lane: globalLane(net, IDX.e, li), s: STOP_BACK });\n  });\n\n  // Opposing stream lanes per approach lane (used by left-turn yield).\n  const group = (road: number, dir: number): number[] =>\n    net.roads[road].lanes.flatMap((lane, li) => (lane.direction === dir ? 690	/** Rotates/translates a road so road.point(atS) lands at the target pose. */
691	function placeAt(road: Road, atS: number, target: { x: number; z: number; hx: number; hz: number }): Transform {
692	  const p = road.point(atS);
693	  // rotY(phi) rotates the xz-plane angle by -phi, so phi = sourceAngle - targetAngle.
694	  const phi = Math.atan2(p.hz, p.hx) - Math.atan2(target.hz, target.hx);
695	  const cos = Math.cos(phi);
696	  const sin = Math.sin(phi);
697	  return {
698	    tx: target.x - (p.x * cos + p.z * sin),
699	    tz: target.z - (-p.x * sin + p.z * cos),
700	    cos,
701	    sin,
702	  };
703	}

```ts
function randomRoute(available: number[]): number {
  if (available.length === 0) return 0;
  if (available.includes(0) && Math.random() < 0.6) return 0;
  const turns = available.filter((r) => r !== 0);
  if (turns.length > 0) return turns[Math.floor(Math.random() * turns.length)];
  return 0;
}

The lane globals in the conflict test (W fwd = 6) and turn tests (N backward = 3) depend on road order — with roadIndex-based construction: all-open order is [s(0-1), n(2-3), e(4-5), w(6-7), nsConn(8-9), ewConn(10-11), arcs(12-19)]. Same as before ✓ so 6 (W fwd) and 3 (N backward) still hold for all-open. But safer to compute from roadIndex: `state.net.laneOffsets[state.roadIndex.n] + 1` for N backward, `state.net.laneOffsets[state.roadIndex.w]` for W forward.
